title: Plant communities in six gradients kept source composition after two to seven years at shared warm sites
abstract: We tested whether co-location removes source composition from warmed plant communities. We used TransPlant data from six elevation gradients, nine source-pair contrasts and six destination locations. Related German designs stayed in one resampling cluster, leaving five clusters. We projected last-census differences between origins onto source-control contrasts from the first common census. After correction for source-control sampling noise, relative cover kept 0.408 of the source contrast (95% cluster bootstrap limits 0.183 to 0.762). Occurrence kept 0.207 (0.124 to 0.385). Absolute cover kept 0.374. All three pooled source signals exceeded an origin-blind label null that preserved known destination blocks. The signal declined over time. An exploratory test gave no clear difference between origins for candidate colonists not detected in source controls. Thus shared broad climate and a nearby species pool did not remove origin information within two to seven years. The study cannot separate persistent residents, soil carryover, genetic differences or local arrival limits. The first source controls are not pre-transplant vegetation. Five clusters and incomplete plot records limit generalization. Code, tests, aggregate evidence, a figure and a retrieval script are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Different source communities retained composition differences after sharing a warmer destination. Last-census source-direction ratios use independent source controls and a correction for control sampling noise. Limits enumerate resamples of five related-design clusters. They do not quantify temperature tracking or prove a permanent state.

citations.reason: Uses its source description and plot preparation rules. Tests a different common-destination contrast in the same field archive.
Its species-specific interval test already covers one proposed extension. Our study tests source information under common destinations instead.
Motivates a test of what remains after reducing long-distance colonist separation. No bird data or estimates are reused.
